name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle
summary: The lunar module that carried the first people to the Moon’s surface. Its descent stage still stands at Tranquility Base.
discoveries: Landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon, the first people to walk on another world.
Its descent stage was the launch pad for the trip home, and it was left behind.

stories.kids: I’m Eagle, the lander that took the first two people to the Moon’s surface. When it was time to go home, my top half flew them up to meet Michael Collins, and my bottom half stayed behind as a launch pad. It’s still at Tranquility Base.
stories.explorer: Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility on July 20, 1969. Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21.6 hours on the surface before the ascent stage lifted off on July 21 at 17:54 UTC. The descent stage remains at Tranquility Base, and the ascent stage was left in lunar orbit.
stories.scientist: The Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle landed at 0.67409° N, 23.47298° E (NASA NSSDC) on 20 July 1969. After a surface stay of 21.6 hours, the ascent stage launched on 21 July 1969 at 17:54 UTC, using the descent stage as its launch platform, and was left in lunar orbit.

clues.prompt: Where on the Moon did I land?
clues.explain: Eagle landed at Tranquility Base, in the Sea of Tranquility.

clues.prompt: How long did the crew stay on the surface?
clues.explain: NASA records a surface stay of 21.6 hours.

clues.prompt: What part of me is still at Tranquility Base?
clues.explain: The descent stage was the launch pad and was left behind.

timeline.title: Launch toward the Moon
timeline.text: Apollo 11 lifts off on a Saturn V rocket with the lunar module Eagle on board.

timeline.title: The Eagle has landed
timeline.text: Armstrong and Aldrin land Eagle in the Sea of Tranquility, and Armstrong radios Houston from Tranquility Base.

timeline.title: Liftoff for home
timeline.text: The ascent stage lifts the crew back into lunar orbit. The descent stage stays on the Moon.

learn.title: Who I am
learn.text: I’m Eagle, the lunar module of Apollo 11. On July 20, 1969, I landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin in the Sea of Tranquility, and Armstrong radioed, “Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.”

learn.title: What I did
learn.text: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21.6 hours on the surface with me. Then my upper half, the ascent stage, lifted them off to rejoin Michael Collins in orbit.

learn.title: Where I am now
learn.text: My lower half, the descent stage, was the launch pad, and it is still standing at Tranquility Base. My upper half was left in lunar orbit.
